## Just what the heck is Blender?

- Open-source, industry leading 3D animation software

::: {.content-visible unless-format="revealjs"}
<!-- will only appear in blogpost -->
Remaining an indie open-source darling for many decades, Blender has gone from 'enthusiast' software to winning [Oscars]() and [Academy Awards]() in the past 5 years.

It would like be a shorter list of things that Blender _can't_ do rather than to list the features that it can. Blender contains two very powerful rendering engines, Cycles & EEVEE. Both have their advantages and disadvantages, we are primarily focused on Cycles for that "cinematic" look

Cycles is a ray-traced "physically based renderer". What that essentially means is that when creating an image, we try to replicate the behaviours of individual photons and how they might behave in a 3D environment. As you might imagine, this is incredibly computationally intensive, but can result in very aesethically pleasing lighting and final rendered results.
:::

## `molecularnodes`

::: {#c99aad95 .cell output-location='slide' execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code code-line-numbers="true"}
import molecularnodes as mn
import MDAnalysis as mda
from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import DCD, PSF, TPR, XTC

canvas = mn.Canvas(mn.scene.Cycles(samples=16))
u = mda.Universe(PSF, DCD)

traj = mn.Trajectory(u).add_style("sphere")

canvas.frame_view(traj)
canvas.snapshot()
```
